AUTHORED, not generated -- transcribed by hand from the clean-room encodings' own disclosures, each entry's basis paraphrasing or quoting the encoding's own prose. Every entry here is a RESIDUE-CANDIDATE per the governing spec's census (§1): a number no relation in this language's current primitive inventory can derive, because the component genuinely has no intrinsic size to probe (a readability judgment) or because the underlying floor is an inherited, never re-derived sentinel. License: Public Domain (The Unlicense), matching research/lyt/__init__.py's license line and the umbrella's ADR-0006 per-file convention. [Fields added 2026-08-13, dispatch B follow-up fix (fresh-context review `lyt-relations-b-review.md` §5): every entry below now carries explicit `widget_ids` (a list, matching facts.generated.json's own '+'-joined multi-widget shape for the six SP_* leaves), `method` (uniformly `read-constant` -- a residue value is, by construction, a documented estimate/constant a human read off a note or a component's own disclosure, never a live playwright probe, so `read-constant`'s own axis-agnostic, source-agnostic lookup shape is the honest fit among the nine primitives, not a repurposing of a mismatched one), and, where landscape/portrait values genuinely differ, `variant`. These are ADDITIVE -- every pre-existing field (`key`, `component`, `value_px`, `axis`, `status`, `basis`) is unchanged; `key` stays the original human-readable descriptive string, now purely documentation, since `widget_ids`/`method`/`variant` are what relations.py's FactsTable.load actually binds to (dispatch A review's own 'bind to the fields, never parse the key string' instruction, now honored for THIS file too, not only facts.generated.json's). Three entries (`side_column_max_cap_340px_component`, `loader.PX_PER_CH`, `WRAPPER_MIN_sentinel`) have no real LYT tree widget to attach to at all (a Split node's own max cap, and two loader-internal constants) -- their `widget_ids` are disclosed SYNTHETIC handles (`sideColumnMaxCap`, `PX_PER_CH`, `WRAPPER_MIN`), not names drawn from any encoding's own census, named as such here rather than left to be discovered as a surprise.]
